purpose: Convert existing first-pass/second-pass judge disagreements into manuscript-facing error categories and claim constraints.

abstention_boundary_reversal.label: Abstention boundary reversed toward correct abstention
abstention_boundary_reversal.manuscript_treatment: Report as unstable abstention-boundary evidence; do not claim abstention calibration is solved.

partial_vs_supported_granularity.label: Partial-support granularity reversed to supported
partial_vs_supported_granularity.manuscript_treatment: Report partial/support boundary as a granularity issue in model-judge labels.

unsupported_to_supported_reversal.label: First-pass unsupported reversed to supported
unsupported_to_supported_reversal.manuscript_treatment: Report as answer-support judge uncertainty; inspect examples before treating unsupported rates as human truth.

manuscript_constraints: Call support/correctness metrics model-judged rather than human-validated.
Report second-pass exact agreement and disagreement taxonomy near any judged-correctness table.
Treat questionable abstentions as unstable boundary cases; do not use them as proof that abstention calibration is solved.
For answer-support claims, highlight that most unsupported-answer and cross-policy cases are stable, but some first-pass unsupported/partial verdicts reverse to supported.
Use Qwen 3B joint-action results to evaluate coverage/support jointly rather than relying on stronger abstention gates alone.

claim_boundary.reason: This taxonomy uses two model judges and no human adjudication; it improves transparency but cannot replace human validation.
